meta.thema: Urban Cycling Infrastructure: Perceived Safety, Route Choice, and Separation Quality

recherche_diagnose.saettigungsgrund: Demonstration sample of validated academic literature and open sensor datasets.

phasen_log.beobachtung: Archetype 1 (Spatial Infrastructure & Urban Mobility) mapped. Platforms: OpenAlex, Zenodo, TRID.
4-facet thesaurus defined (cycling infrastructure, subjective safety, commuter groups, qualitative/sensor methods).
OpenAlex REST API query executed with per-page=50; returned 112 raw hits.
Harvested in-depth cyclist ride-along interviews and open surface roughness datasets.
Quality gate passed; non-empirical opinion pieces excluded.

findings.titel: Perceived safety and stress factors among urban bicycle commuters: A mixed-methods ride-along study
findings.abstract_kurzfassung: Investigates subjective stress and route detours among urban cyclists using 28 semi-structured ride-along interviews and GPS tracking. Demonstrates that physical barrier separation reduces stress indicators by over 40% compared to painted on-street lanes.
findings.relevanz_begruendung: Empirical evidence on user resistance and perceived safety thresholds across separated vs. shared cycling corridors.

daten_anhaenge.titel_beschreibung: Semi-structured ride-along interview guide and coding scheme (ESM Appendix A)

findings.titel: Bicycle surface quality and vibration dataset: Accelerometer and route telemetry across urban corridors
findings.abstract_kurzfassung: Open-access dataset recording 3-axis accelerometer and GPS data from 50 test cyclists across asphalt, cobblestone, and segregated concrete cycle paths, paired with post-ride comfort surveys.
findings.relevanz_begruendung: Provides concrete roughness indices and vibration comfort thresholds needed for surface specification in cycling network planning.

daten_anhaenge.titel_beschreibung: Calibrated 3-axis accelerometer and GPS track files (CSV format)
